concept_html:
A schema states what a DataFrame must look like: which columns exist, their dtypes, and rules on their values. pandera checks a pandas DataFrame against a schema and raises when it does not match. Examples here use pandera 0.33 with pandas 3.

import pandera.pandas as pa

RESPONSES = pa.DataFrameSchema(
    {
        "respondent_id": pa.Column(str, unique=True),
        "age": pa.Column(int, pa.Check.in_range(16, 99)),
        "weight": pa.Column(float, pa.Check.gt(0)),
    },
    strict=True,
    coerce=True,
)
clean = RESPONSES.validate(raw, lazy=True)
  • pa.Column(dtype, checks, nullable=False) is the default: nulls fail unless you set nullable=True.
  • unique=True rejects duplicate keys.
  • strict=True rejects columns the schema does not name. coerce=True converts dtypes before checking.
  • lazy=True collects every failure into one SchemaErrors exception. Its failure_cases attribute is a DataFrame with the column, check and failing value. Without lazy, validation stops at the first SchemaError.

SchemaErrors is not a subclass of SchemaError. Catch both when you handle failures. A strict=True violation raises SchemaErrors even without lazy=True.

The class syntax, pa.DataFrameModel, does the same with type hints. Add @pa.check_types to a function whose parameters are annotated DataFrame[Model], and pandera validates inputs and outputs on every call.

Import from pandera.pandas. The plain import pandera still works in 0.33, but the pandas-specific module is the documented path.

pandera does not run in this app's browser runtime. The exercises check your code's structure. Run pytest locally with the dev group to execute schemas for real.

import pandas as pd
import pandera.pandas as pa

schema = pa.DataFrameSchema({"w": pa.Column(float, pa.Check.gt(0))})
try:
    schema.validate(pd.DataFrame({"w": [1.0, -2.0, -3.0]}), lazy=True)
except pa.errors.SchemaErrors as err:
    print(err.failure_cases["failure_case"].tolist())

import pandas as pd
import pandera.pandas as pa

SCORES = pa.DataFrameSchema(
    {
        "respondent_id": pa.Column(str, unique=True),
        "nps": pa.Column(int, pa.Check.in_range(0, 10)),
        "comment": pa.Column(str, nullable=True),
    },
    strict=True,
    coerce=True,
)


def validate_scores(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Validate an NPS extract. Grain: one row per respondent.

    Raises:
        pa.errors.SchemaErrors: With every failing check.
    """
    return SCORES.validate(df, lazy=True)

title: DataFrame schemas with pandera
why_html:
A supplier changes a weight export so that non-responders get weight 0 instead of being left out. The weighting script divides by the sum of weights per cell. Three cells now contain only zeros. The script writes NaN shares to the client dashboard, and nobody sees an error.

pa.Column(float, pa.Check.gt(0)) on the input fails the run on day one, with the failing rows listed in failure_cases.
